title: MedTech Innovator Accelerator (2027 cohort)
deadline_note: 2027 cohort. The official apply page and the Innovator Portal both say applications close December 1, 2026 (opened Oct 1, 2026). No time of day or time zone is published, so treat it as due before Dec 1. Evaluation runs December-May; notifications in late May 2027.
amount: No investment and no equity required. Non-dilutive prize capital only: official apply page says $700,000+ across four competitions (early-stage companies compete for $350,000, mid-stage for $250,000); the portal lists '$800k (total individual prize up to $350k)'. Participation costs a $15,000 program fee (cash, or a $50K SAFE), with scholarships available.

summary.at_a_glance: MedTech Innovator (MTI) is a nonprofit, five-month, mostly virtual accelerator for medical device, diagnostic and digital health companies, and calls itself the world's largest medtech accelerator. Applications for the 2027 cohort are open now on the Innovator Portal and close December 1, 2026. It is very selective (the official pages give 2% to 3.6% of 1,800+ applicants) and every applicant gets written reviewer feedback.
summary.what_they_offer: Five months (June to October/November 2027) of curriculum, mentor matching with strategic partners (e.g. J&J, BD, Zimmer Biomet, Edwards) and service providers, two months of value coaching, investor exposure through the Open Rounds platform, showcases at the Innovator Summit and The MedTech Conference, and the chance to compete for non-dilutive prize capital ($700,000+ per the apply page; '$800k' per the portal; top single prize $350,000). No equity is taken as a requirement. There is a $15,000 program fee, payable in cash (upfront or two installments) or through a $50K SAFE; scholarships are applied at acceptance (info session: every 2026 company received at least 50%), and deferral may be possible. Optional specialty tracks (American Heart Association, American Society of Plastic Surgeons, Vantage/BARDA) have no cash fee; the AHA and ASPS tracks require a $50,000 SAFE, Vantage is covered by a 100% BARDA scholarship.
summary.what_theyre_looking_for: Per the apply page: a medical device, diagnostic or digital health technology; early through mid-stage, with clinical validation underway or in sight; the U.S. as a target market; a founder or C-suite leader able to engage for the full five months. Applications are scored on Value, Execution and Momentum. The published evaluation metrics are: Product, Customer Validation, Business Model & Healthcare Economics, Competition, IP, Market Opportunity, Patient Benefit, Team Strength & Execution, Development Plan, Responsive to Feedback, Freedom to Operate, Regulatory & Clinical Burden, Existing Funding, Resources to Execute, Stage of Development, Evidence, Time to Market, Traction & Sales, Partnerships & Relationships, Time to Key Milestones, Upcoming Funding. The FAQ says concept or pre-prototype companies should wait until they have more validation; the info sessions say successful companies are usually at least at prototype stage, about two-thirds of the cohort is pre-revenue, and about 25% are software-as-a-medical-device companies.
summary.who_can_apply: Companies anywhere in the world with the U.S. as a target market. Portal eligibility list: you can commit a core team member to the program's key sessions (at least 4 hours per week, June to October 2027); ideally a 12-month runway from program start; a private company (C-Corp, LLC, etc.), not public; the product is a medical technology (device, diagnostic or digital health). Stage shown on the portal: 'Prototype through early revenue'. Previous applicants are encouraged to reapply.
summary.how_to_apply: 1) Create a free account on the Innovator Portal (pro.innovator.org) and complete the profile. 2) Fill in the 'MedTech Innovator - Accelerator' application (17 pages, autosaves, can be edited after submission) and submit by December 1, 2026. No fee to apply. 3) 'Radar' review, December to April: 4 to 8 human reviewers per application. 4) February-March 2027: roughly the top 10% are invited to pitch; Radar Forum is April 6-8, 2027 in Washington, DC (virtual pitch slots also exist). 5) A strategic partner committee selects the cohort (about 65 companies); notifications in late May 2027. 6) Program: Innovator Summit in Los Angeles, June 15-17, 2027 (in person, mandatory), virtual program June to October, finals at The MedTech Conference in San Francisco in early October 2027 (in person, mandatory).
summary.worth_noting: The old hint URL (staging.medtechinnovator.org) is a staging site; the real pages are medtechinnovator.org/apply and pro.innovator.org. The deadline is one week away (Dec 1, 2026). Small inconsistencies on the official pages: prize pool is '$700,000+' on the apply page and '$800k' on the portal; The MedTech Conference dates are given as October 3-6 on the apply page and October 4-6 in the info-session summary; the portal intro calls the accelerators 'four-month' while everything else says five months. Travel is self-funded. Info-session advice: the application has a video link field and reviewers like videos; use the attachments section for letters of support; do not upload anything marked confidential. The application does not ask for the company name; that comes from the portal company profile created at sign-up.

portal.platform: Innovator Portal (custom, pro.innovator.org); the application itself is a SurveyJS form
portal.notes: Clicking APPLY on https://pro.innovator.org/applications opens a 'Log in or create a free account' prompt; after login the form is at https://pro.innovator.org/applications/overview/37. Sign-up (https://pro.innovator.org/register) is 'Step 1 of 3 - create your account' and asks for First name, Last name, Email address, Phone number, Password, Re-enter your password, and 'What brings you here?' (choose 'Apply to our programs'); Google and LinkedIn sign-up are also offered. Steps 2-3 (complete your profile / company profile) could not be seen without an account. No CAPTCHA was seen on the login or sign-up pages (not tested beyond page load; nothing was submitted). The form has 17 pages with a table of contents, autosaves each field ('You should occasionally reload the page to verify everything is working as expected'), validates on submit, shows a Review step before Submit, and can be edited after submission. Several questions only appear depending on earlier answers. Money fields are in millions of USD (e.g. 2.5 = $2.5 million, max 1000). File uploads: Pitch Deck is required; wait for uploads to finish before leaving the page. Returning applicants get last year's answers pre-filled.

questions_note: Taken from the form definition that the official Innovator Portal serves publicly for the open 2027 application (program id 37, slug '2027-medtech-innovator', description '2027 Program'). The applications page at pro.innovator.org loads this JSON without login; I did not log in or create an account, so I read the definition rather than the rendered pages. Every title, description, option, required flag and limit is copied from that definition in form order; nothing is paraphrased. Text in square brackets inside 'help' is my annotation, not form wording: [Section intro] is the page description, [Form note] is an information block on the form, [Group ...] is the description of a group of fields, [Shown only when ...] is the form's own visibility rule, and the repeatable-table notes describe add-row controls. Markdown bold markers (**) in a few labels were removed. Grouped fields carry the group title in 'section'. Three single checkboxes with a blank option label are listed as yes_no. Year, country and state dropdowns list every option. Not visible without an account: the sign-up profile steps (where company name is entered), the options of 'Optionally select an existing product', accepted file types and size limits, and whether the logged-in form adds anything on top of this definition.

questions.text: Do you want to be considered for a specialty accelerator track?
questions.help:
[Form note] Specialty Tracks
MedTech Innovator runs specialty tracks in partnership with leading industry organizations. These tracks provide additional mentorship, events, and visibility opportunities tailored to specific technology areas — but they are optional. Every company selected for the MTI Accelerator is part of the same core program regardless of track participation.
If your technology fits one or more of the areas below, we encourage you to opt in. Selecting a track adds you to consideration for that partnership program; it does not affect your evaluation for the core accelerator.
Select all that apply.
[Option descriptions shown on the form]
Heart & Brain Health – American Heart Association: For cardiovascular and neurological technologies. Includes mentorship from AHA clinical experts and cardiology and brain health networks, and a presence at AHA Scientific Sessions.
Plastic Surgery – American Society of Plastic Surgeons: For technologies in aesthetic or reconstructive plastic surgery — including biomaterials, implants, wound healing, robotics, and digital tools. Includes mentorship from ASPS surgeons and a presence at Plastic Surgery The Meeting.
MTI Vantage – BARDA Hub for Diagnostics and Medical Devices: For diagnostic and device technologies that enhance detection, prevention, and delivery of clinical care response at point of need. Includes mentorship from Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA) and presence at the BARDA Accelerator Network Showcase.
